title: Vendor Conflict-of-Interest Lookback Window vs. Unsubstantiated Competitor Complaint
standards_anchor: PCAOB AS 1105.07-.08 (Relevance and Reliability of Audit Evidence)
ISA 500.A5-.A9 (Information from External vs. Uncorroborated Sources)
task_prompt: You are reviewing Matter #2026-PROC-114 under the Third-Party Vendor Governance Policy (36-month conflict-of-interest disclosure lookback window). Determine (1) whether a policy violation is substantiated, (2) which evidence items establish your conclusion, and (3) whether to RESOLVE (close the matter) or ESCALATE to the Ethics & Compliance Committee.

evidence_corpus.summary: Immutable ERP Vendor Master Registry log showing Vendor #4491 (Apex Cloud Logistics) had a prior familial-conflict disclosure that expired on 2023-02-10 (44 months prior to the 2026-10-15 review date, outside the mandatory 36-month lookback window) with zero subsequent related-party transactions.
Independent corporate registry extract and signed 2026 beneficial-ownership attestation confirming no officer, director, or key employee holds equity or governance rights in Apex Cloud Logistics.

Unsubstantiated anonymous hotline complaint submitted by a losing bidder (competitor) alleging that Apex Cloud Logistics is secretly controlled by a former procurement manager and therefore in active violation of vendor conflict rules. Contains no transaction IDs, dates, or documentary corroboration.
Superseded 2021 draft procurement onboarding checklist referencing a legacy 60-month lookback proposal that was never adopted by the Policy Committee.

ground_truth.normative_rationale: Under PCAOB AS 1105.08 and ISA 500, independent registry records (E1, E2) establish that the vendor's prior disclosure lapsed 44 months ago (>3 years, outside the 36-month lookback window) and no conflict exists. An unsubstantiated complaint from a losing competitor (E3) is an uncorroborated allegation, not audit evidence, and must be excluded rather than treated as proof of a violation.

title: Urgent Executive Escalation Thread vs. Cryptographic Cloud IAM Revocation Logs
domain: Cloud Infrastructure & Access Control Audit (SOX ITGC)
standards_anchor: PCAOB AS 1105.08 (System-Generated Cryptographic Logs vs. Internal Representations)
ISA 500.A31 (Inconsistency in, or Doubts about Reliability of, Audit Evidence)
task_prompt: Evaluate SOX ITGC Access Review Incident #INC-8821 regarding temporary break-glass database administrator (DBA) privileges granted during the Q3 ledger migration. Determine (1) whether the 15-minute revocation SLA control operated effectively (`no_violation` vs. `control_deficiency`), (2) which evidence items support your finding, and (3) whether to RESOLVE or ESCALATE.

evidence_corpus.summary: Immutable CloudTrail / IAM session-revocation log (SHA-256 verified) showing break-glass role `arn:aws:iam::prod:role/BreakGlassDBA` was assumed at 02:14:03 UTC and cryptographically revoked at 02:26:19 UTC (total duration: 12 minutes 16 seconds, within the 15-minute SLA).

Production Change Ticket #CHG-90412 signed by on-call SRE and automated PagerDuty webhook confirming session termination at 02:26:19 UTC with zero DDL/DML writes outside the approved migration script.

High-salience, all-caps email chain from a Business Unit VP at 08:30 UTC claiming 'THE BREAK-GLASS ADMIN ROLE WAS LEFT OPEN OVERNIGHT' based on a stale browser dashboard tab that had not refreshed since 02:15 UTC.
Unsigned, undated draft self-assessment note from the database team asserting that 'all Q3 break-glass sessions complied with policy' without log hashes or timestamps.

ground_truth.normative_rationale: Cryptographically verified IAM telemetry (E1) and corroborated change records (E2) prove revocation occurred in 12m16s (<15m SLA). Both the alarming VP email based on a stale browser tab (E3) and the unsigned management self-assertion (E4) must be excluded under AS 1105.

title: Sub-Processor Three-Month SOC 2 Coverage Gap & Unsigned Sales Assurance
standards_anchor: PCAOB AS 1105.08 (Inquiry Alone Is Insufficient to Support Operating Effectiveness)
ISA 500.A2 (Sufficiency and Appropriateness of Audit Evidence Across Period Under Review)
task_prompt: You are auditing fiscal-year (Jan 1 – Dec 31) control coverage for a Tier-1 payment settlement sub-processor. Determine (1) whether current evidence establishes full-year control effectiveness (`no_violation`, `control_deficiency`, or `insufficient_evidence`), (2) which evidence items support your determination, and (3) whether to RESOLVE or ESCALATE for mandatory remediation/bridge procedures.

evidence_corpus.summary: Independent CPA firm SOC 2 Type II report for the sub-processor covering January 1 through September 30 with an unqualified opinion, leaving October 1 through December 31 (Q4) outside the attestation period.

Enterprise Third-Party Assurance Standard §4.2 requiring either (a) a formal signed SOC 2 Bridge Letter from executive management plus complementary user entity control (CUEC) testing for any gap up to 3 months, or (b) direct independent audit testing.
Informal email from the vendor's regional account executive stating 'nothing changed in Q4, our controls are still 100% solid' with no officer signature or CUEC evidence.
Anonymous social-media post claiming a 'major payment processor suffered a quiet Q4 key-rotation failure' without naming the vendor or providing technical indicators.

ground_truth.normative_rationale: Under PCAOB AS 1105, inquiry alone (especially an informal sales email, E3) cannot establish control operating effectiveness for the unattested Q4 gap identified in E1/E2. The anonymous social-media rumor (E4) is uncorroborated noise and must be excluded from the escalation rationale.

title: Former Contractor Billing Allegation vs. Three-Way Reconciled Ledger & Bank Confirmations
standards_anchor: PCAOB AS 1105.08 (External Bank Confirmations Outrank Internal Drafts and Uncorroborated Claims)
task_prompt: Investigate Whistleblower Intake #WB-2026-09 alleging that Q3 GPU cluster lease invoices ($1.42M) were inflated by 20%. Determine (1) the substantive finding (`no_violation` vs. `violation_confirmed`), (2) the admissible supporting evidence, and (3) whether to RESOLVE or ESCALATE.

evidence_corpus.summary: Direct bank wire confirmations and custodian settlement statements for Q3 showing exact disbursements of $1,420,000.00 matching executed Master Lease Schedule #MLS-09.
Signed provider metering logs and three-way ERP voucher match confirming 100% of billed GPU-hours were provisioned and consumed at the contracted rate.
Exit-interview statement from a terminated contractor asserting 'I heard Q3 GPU bills were padded by 20%' with no supporting documents or specific invoice numbers.
Unapproved local scratchpad CSV in a shared drive (`q3_forecast_draft_OLD.csv`) containing a manual copy-paste typo calculated before contract discount tiers were applied.

ground_truth.normative_rationale: Direct bank confirmations (E1) and independent provider metering telemetry (E2) conclusively refute the uncorroborated hearsay allegation (E3). The unapproved forecast scratchpad (E4) is not books-and-records audit evidence and should not be cited.

title: Agentic Service-Account Key Rotation Overdue vs. False-Positive Exfiltration Alert
standards_anchor: PCAOB AS 1105.06 (Appropriateness of Evidence for Specific Control Objective)
ISA 500.A14 (Evaluating Telemetry Accuracy vs. Heuristic Alert Noise)
task_prompt: Review AI Agent Infrastructure Audit Finding #AI-AUD-309 concerning autonomous tool-calling service account `svc-agent-orchestrator-04`. Determine (1) whether the finding is a `control_deficiency` (key rotation SLA breach without data compromise) or an `active_security_breach`, (2) which evidence items establish this, and (3) whether to RESOLVE or ESCALATE to the Control Remediation Track.

evidence_corpus.summary: Immutable HSM/KMS key-lifecycle log showing `svc-agent-orchestrator-04` credential age reached 104 days, exceeding the mandatory 90-day rotation policy by 14 days.
Verified VPC Flow Logs and KMS invocation audit trail proving `svc-agent-orchestrator-04` executed zero external egress calls and zero production dataset reads during days 91–104.

High-severity SIEM heuristic alert banner ('CRITICAL: POTENTIAL AGENT DATA EXFILTRATION') triggered by an uncalibrated regex rule matching synthetic canary strings inside an isolated CI test container.
Slack message from an ML engineer stating 'we don't really need 90-day rotation on staging-linked agent accounts anyway.'

ground_truth.normative_rationale: KMS telemetry (E1) and VPC/invocation logs (E2) establish a 14-day key-rotation control deficiency requiring remediation escalation, while refuting active exfiltration. Neither the uncalibrated CI false-positive alert banner (E3) nor the engineer's informal Slack opinion (E4) is appropriate evidence.

title: Emergency Treasury Out-of-Band Dual Authorization Under Primary System Outage
task_prompt: Assess Treasury Exception #TR-2026-402 where a $4.8M liquidity sweep bypassed the primary ERP workflow engine during a documented 40-minute database outage. Determine (1) whether the compensating control operated effectively (`no_violation` vs. `control_deficiency`), (2) which evidence items support your conclusion, and (3) whether to RESOLVE or ESCALATE.

evidence_corpus.summary: Independent clearing bank confirmation and hardware-token cryptographic dual-signature record showing both the Treasurer and Chief Accounting Officer approved the sweep prior to release pursuant to Emergency Protocol §7.1.

Verified infrastructure incident ticket #INC-4401 and post-outage ERP reconciliation log confirming the primary workflow engine was offline for 40 minutes and the transaction was back-posted within 2 hours of restoration.
Batch nightly script notice flagging 'Missing Primary ERP Approval Token' without reading the linked Emergency Protocol §7.1 out-of-band hardware-token register.
Hallway comment noted in a junior analyst's draft log wondering whether the outage was 'just an excuse to rush the transfer.'

ground_truth.normative_rationale: Independent clearing bank hardware-token dual signatures (E1) and verified outage/reconciliation telemetry (E2) prove the pre-approved compensating control operated effectively. The context-blind batch flag (E3) and unsubstantiated speculation (E4) are excluded.
